walkthroughs.body_html:
A steep gradient = fast rate.

Gradient = rise ÷ run. A flat region = no change. Draw a tangent for the rate at one moment on a curve.

Identify with a ring. Repeat that data point if possible.

Decide whether to exclude it before calculating means — say so in your evaluation.

State: was the result reliable (close repeats)? Was the method valid (correct measurement)? What would you change next time?

mcqs.q: What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.
Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.

mcqs.q: During an action potential, do Na+ and K+ move through the same channels?
options: Na+ and K+ swap places through the same channel at the same time.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.
No — voltage-gated Na+ channels open first (depolarisation, Na+ in), then voltage-gated K+ channels open (repolarisation, K+ out).

mcqs.q: What is the main role of mitochondria in a cell?
options: Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
To carry out aerobic respiration, producing ATP that cells use as an energy currency.
Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.
Mitochondria produce energy by creating it from nothing.
